# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 107 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 107 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_107_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 24

**1** I asked him about the seasons and why the tower was not built on a level plain but upon a rock and upon water. **2** He said to me, "You are right to inquire about the foundation of the tower. **3** I asked him the reason it was built upon water, and he said to me: 'I have told you before, and yet you still ask. Your inquiry is good; listen. **4** The rock and the water are one. The rock is the Son of God. He existed before all creation, and he appeared in the last days of this present age. **5** The water also was before all creation; this is why water serves for cleansing and entry into eternal life, for the earth was created by water. **6** Therefore the rock is ancient and the water is new; but through baptism men enter the kingdom of God and are cleansed from their sins and defilements through the name of the Son of God. **7** The rock and the water are one; they are inseparable. Whoever comes to God must pass through both: through water to be cleansed, and through the rock to stand firm. **8** The foundation of all life is one: the Son of God.'"

---

### Translator's Note
This is the theological finale of Similitude 9 — the synthesis of rock (pre-existent Son) and water (baptism) as the single, inseparable foundation of the Church and of eternal life. The two requirements stated throughout — the Name and the water — are here revealed to be one reality: the Son of God, encountered through baptism into his Name. "The foundation of all life is one: the Son of God" (v. 8) is arguably the most concentrated theological statement in the entire Shepherd. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
